intro_html: Provencal cooking is the sunny end of French food: tomatoes, olives, capers, garlic, and herbs, without a drop of cream anywhere. Chicken thighs braise with burst cherry tomatoes until the sauce is bright and briny rather than heavy, which makes this one of the few French dishes that does not feel like a weight on the plate. Each bowl runs 568 calories and 46 grams of protein for about $3.84 a serving (at everyday cost).
cost_closing_html: About $3.84 a bowl (at everyday cost). Cherry tomatoes and olives are the notable lines, and both are the reason this tastes like the south of France instead of like generic braised chicken.
shop_smart: Cherry tomatoes cost more per pound than canned, but here they are structural. They burst and make the sauce while staying whole enough to bite. This is the rare case where fresh is worth the difference.
Capers and olives are shelf stable jars used in small amounts, so the cost per batch is modest and neither one spoils while you get around to the next recipe.
Boneless thighs are the cheapest good chicken in the store and they do not dry out in a braise. That is why they show up in nearly every recipe in this batch.
Italian seasoning is a blend you can approximate from oregano, basil, and thyme jars you already own. Buying the blend is convenient, not required.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Season the chicken thighs with salt, pepper, and italian seasoning and brown them in the olive oil in batches. Set them aside.
Cook the sliced onions in the same pan until soft and lightly browned, then add the garlic for a minute.
Add the cherry tomatoes whole and cook over medium-high heat until they blister and start to burst, about 6 minutes. Press a few with the back of a spoon to get things moving.
Pour in the chicken broth and scrape the bottom of the pan, then return the chicken with any juices.
Simmer uncovered 25 to 30 minutes, until the chicken is tender and the sauce has reduced enough to cling instead of run.
Add the olives and capers in the last 5 minutes. Adding them early makes the whole pot too salty, and once that happens there is no way back.
Cook the rice, then taste the sauce and adjust the salt, keeping in mind the olives brought their own.
portion_html: Weigh the rice into each container, then set the pan on the scale, subtract the empty weight you wrote down, and divide by 14. Spoon tomatoes and olives into every container rather than letting them all land in the first three. Each portion lands at 568 calories.

recipeIngredient: Pantry: italian seasoning, salt, black pepper
steps: Season and brown the chicken thighs in olive oil, then set aside.
Soften the onions and add the garlic.
Blister the cherry tomatoes until they burst.
Add the broth, return the chicken, and simmer uncovered 25 to 30 minutes.
Stir in the olives and capers for the last 5 minutes.
Cook the rice and weigh both into 14 containers.
